# How to Turn Sales Conversations into Actionable Briefs with AI

> **In short:** Record your sales call, export the transcript, upload it to ChatGPT with a clear prompt, and paste the resulting summary straight into your CRM (customer relationship management software — the place where you track every deal and contact). The whole process takes about 10 minutes after each call.

You just hung up from a 45-minute sales call. Your notes are scattered, your next call is in 30 minutes, and you still need to update your CRM. Sound familiar?

AI can do the heavy lifting here. With a transcript and a clear prompt (the instructions you give the AI), ChatGPT will hand you a structured brief in seconds. Here's how to set it up so you can do this after every call.

## What you'll need

- A meeting platform with recording and transcription. Zoom (Pro plan or higher), Microsoft Teams (with transcription enabled), or Google Meet on Google Workspace all work. Some of these are paid features — check your plan before your next call.
- A free ChatGPT account at chatgpt.com. The free tier accepts text you paste in. Uploading files works more smoothly on ChatGPT Plus.
- About 10 minutes after each call.

## Step 1 — Record your call and turn it into text

Open Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or Google Meet as usual and join your call. Before anyone starts talking, look for the **Record** button — in Zoom and Teams it sits in the bottom toolbar; in Google Meet it lives in the three-dot menu at the bottom right of the screen.

Click Record to start. Once the call ends, open the recording (Zoom emails you a link, Teams shows it in the meeting chat, Google Meet saves it to Google Drive). Look for the transcript file alongside the recording — most platforms now generate one automatically, but if not, transcription may need to be turned on in your settings first.

💬 *Example file name:* "Acme Corp — Discovery Call — June 4, 2026"

**You'll know it worked when:** you see a transcript file (usually .txt or .vtt) next to your recording.

## Step 2 — Export the transcript to your computer

Open the transcript page from Step 1 and look for a **Download** or **Export** button. Save the file as a plain text (.txt) or Word (.docx) document to your desktop so you can find it easily.

Give the file a descriptive name with the company and date, like *AcmeCorp_2026-06-04.txt*. This helps you stay organized and gives the AI useful context about which call it's reading.

**You'll know it worked when:** the file is on your computer and opens in any text editor, showing speaker names followed by what they said.

## Step 3 — Open ChatGPT and start a fresh chat

Open your browser and go to chatgpt.com, or launch the ChatGPT app. Sign in with the account you usually use.

Click **New chat** at the top of the left sidebar (it shows as a pencil icon or a button labeled "New chat"). Starting a fresh conversation — rather than continuing an old one — keeps the AI focused on this single call instead of mixing it up with past context.

**You'll know it worked when:** you see a clean message box at the bottom of the screen with no prior conversation above it.

## Step 4 — Add your transcript to the chat

In the message box, click the **paperclip** or **attachment** icon (it sits just to the left of the text field on desktop). Select your transcript file from the window that opens. You'll see the file name appear above the message box.

If your plan doesn't allow file uploads, open the transcript on your computer, press Ctrl+A (or Cmd+A on Mac) to select everything, copy it with Ctrl+C, then paste it directly into the message box instead.

**You'll know it worked when:** the file name shows under the message box, or you see the transcript text appear inside the chat.

## Step 5 — Send a clear, structured prompt

Type your instructions in the same message, right after the transcript. The clearer your prompt, the better your output. Here's one you can copy and adapt:

💬 *"I'm a sales rep. Read this call transcript and give me: (1) a 3-bullet summary of decisions, next steps, and open questions; (2) a pipeline update with current stage, win likelihood, and forecast close date; (3) a next-action list with names and deadlines. Keep each section short — I need to paste this into my CRM."*

Press Enter or click the send arrow. ChatGPT usually responds within 10–30 seconds with three clearly labeled sections.

**You'll know it worked when:** ChatGPT returns three sections matching what you asked for, and you can read each one in under a minute.

## Step 6 — Review the output and paste it into your CRM

Before you copy anything, read through ChatGPT's response. AI can mishear names, mix up numbers, or invent details that weren't said. A 30-second scan catches most mistakes.

When it looks right, click the small **copy** icon at the bottom of ChatGPT's response. Then open your CRM and paste each section into the right field — summary in the notes, pipeline update in the deal record, action items in the task list.

**You'll know it worked when:** your CRM shows a clean, structured brief instead of your usual messy notes — and your next call starts on time.

## Common mistakes

- **Skipping the review step.** AI sometimes invents details that sound plausible but weren't actually said. Always spend 30 seconds checking names, numbers, and dates against the original transcript.
- **Using a vague prompt.** Asking for "a summary" gives you a paragraph. Asking for "a 3-bullet summary with named sections" gives you something you can paste straight into your CRM fields.
- **Forgetting to enable transcription ahead of time.** Some platforms disable it by default. Check your settings *before* your next call — old audio recordings can't be transcribed retroactively without extra processing.
- **Uploading a sensitive call without checking your company's AI policy.** Some employers restrict what data can go into public AI tools. Confirm with your manager before you upload customer conversations.

## What this means for you

- **If you're a sales rep:** Pick one call this week and try this end-to-end. Once you've done it twice, the 10 minutes after each call becomes a habit — and you'll never go back to messy notes.
- **If you lead a sales team:** Standardize on one prompt template so everyone's briefs come out in the same format. Pipeline reviews get easier when the structure is consistent across the team.
- **If you're new to AI:** You don't need to learn prompt engineering (the skill of writing careful AI instructions) to start. One good template, used consistently, beats a clever prompt used once.

## Wrap-up

The whole flow is: record, export, upload, prompt, review, paste. Ten minutes of admin becomes two. Start with your next call this afternoon.
